result.summary: DO-NOT-SHIP: pass 9 found three blocking broker ownership races and two Windows recovery failures in the branch diff against main.

findings.title: 1. [BLOCKING] Grace expiry can erase a live broker with no recorded PID
findings.body: If the failed-start kill cannot stop the child and the follow-up PID save fails, abandonStart logs the failure but leaves a pid-null starting record. After 60 seconds, this path treats the missing PID as settled, removes the record and files, and starts a replacement without proving the old child exited. A still-running broker then has no exclusion record and can be included in a later worker-tree kill.
findings.recommendation: Require verified child exit or broker self-registration of PID and identity before clearing a pid-null record; elapsed time alone must not settle it.

findings.title: 2. [BLOCKING] Failed-start cleanup can kill a broker another caller adopted
findings.body: A starter can time out waiting for the endpoint just as it begins answering. Another caller can promote that starting record to ready and use it, but abandonStart never rechecks or reserves the claim before killing the child. It can terminate the adopted broker during an active turn, then clear its ready record by endpoint; if the kill fails, its endpoint-only save can demote the ready record to starting.
findings.recommendation: Reserve failed-start teardown under the state lock and refuse the kill if the claim was promoted or otherwise changed.

findings.title: 3. [BLOCKING] An expired replacing reservation can be promoted before its owner kills
findings.body: If a replacer is suspended for over 60 seconds after reserving teardown, another caller may find the recovered endpoint, promote the replacing record to ready, and remove its nonce. The original replacer can then resume its kill outside the lock; nonce-guarded clearing fails, leaving a ready record for a broker it just killed and disrupting its new client. This depends on a long process pause, not a normal 4-second kill.
findings.recommendation: Do not let time alone transfer a replacing claim while its owner can resume; fence the kill against promotion or prove the owner has stopped.

findings.title: 4. [SHOULD-FIX] A fresh Windows broker can become ready without identity
findings.body: The fresh-start path saves and returns a ready session even when the Windows identity probe returned null. Later calls reuse that ready record without probing again. Worker cancellation then refuses the broker exclusion, and SessionEnd keeps the broker, even if the probe failure was transient.
findings.recommendation: Keep the record starting and use direct transport on Windows until its identity is recorded; retry promotion on a later call.

findings.title: 5. [SHOULD-FIX] Adoption holds the workspace lock during a Windows probe
findings.body: Adoption calls getProcessIdentity inside withStateLock. Its PowerShell probe can consume 10 seconds, exceeding the 5-second default lock wait used by cancel and the SessionEnd lock step. A stalled probe can therefore make cancellation fail to acquire the lock and make SessionEnd defer cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Probe outside the lock, then reacquire it and compare the full claim before promoting.

next_steps: Fix the three ownership transitions before release and add interleaving tests for each.
Verify Windows identity recovery and lock contention with the broker and cancel end-to-end paths.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP: pass 9 found three blocking broker ownership races and two Windows recovery failures in the branch diff against main.

Findings:
- [high] 1. [BLOCKING] Grace expiry can erase a live broker with no recorded PID (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:386-390)
  If the failed-start kill cannot stop the child and the follow-up PID save fails, abandonStart logs the failure but leaves a pid-null starting record. After 60 seconds, this path treats the missing PID as settled, removes the record and files, and starts a replacement without proving the old child exited. A still-running broker then has no exclusion record and can be included in a later worker-tree kill.
  Recommendation: Require verified child exit or broker self-registration of PID and identity before clearing a pid-null record; elapsed time alone must not settle it.
- [high] 2. [BLOCKING] Failed-start cleanup can kill a broker another caller adopted (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:526-555)
  A starter can time out waiting for the endpoint just as it begins answering. Another caller can promote that starting record to ready and use it, but abandonStart never rechecks or reserves the claim before killing the child. It can terminate the adopted broker during an active turn, then clear its ready record by endpoint; if the kill fails, its endpoint-only save can demote the ready record to starting.
  Recommendation: Reserve failed-start teardown under the state lock and refuse the kill if the claim was promoted or otherwise changed.
- [high] 3. [BLOCKING] An expired replacing reservation can be promoted before its owner kills (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:341-355)
  If a replacer is suspended for over 60 seconds after reserving teardown, another caller may find the recovered endpoint, promote the replacing record to ready, and remove its nonce. The original replacer can then resume its kill outside the lock; nonce-guarded clearing fails, leaving a ready record for a broker it just killed and disrupting its new client. This depends on a long process pause, not a normal 4-second kill.
  Recommendation: Do not let time alone transfer a replacing claim while its owner can resume; fence the kill against promotion or prove the owner has stopped.
- [medium] 4. [SHOULD-FIX] A fresh Windows broker can become ready without identity (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:570-584)
  The fresh-start path saves and returns a ready session even when the Windows identity probe returned null. Later calls reuse that ready record without probing again. Worker cancellation then refuses the broker exclusion, and SessionEnd keeps the broker, even if the probe failure was transient.
  Recommendation: Keep the record starting and use direct transport on Windows until its identity is recorded; retry promotion on a later call.
- [medium] 5. [SHOULD-FIX] Adoption holds the workspace lock during a Windows probe (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:345-364)
  Adoption calls getProcessIdentity inside withStateLock. Its PowerShell probe can consume 10 seconds, exceeding the 5-second default lock wait used by cancel and the SessionEnd lock step. A stalled probe can therefore make cancellation fail to acquire the lock and make SessionEnd defer cleanup.
  Recommendation: Probe outside the lock, then reacquire it and compare the full claim before promoting.

Next steps:
- Fix the three ownership transitions before release and add interleaving tests for each.
- Verify Windows identity recovery and lock contention with the broker and cancel end-to-end paths.
